analysis:
The only change in this PR is to docs/developer/test.md, in the CI caching paragraph around base lines 142-146 and head lines 142-153. It makes two documentation edits. CI cache saving is now described as push-only for dev/master, with pull requests restoring the base branch's entry and saving nothing. It also adds a note that the MiMo audio gate (testNativeAudioRelease) runs only when its inputs change or on master pushes. The supplied units (base lines 2304-3100) are unchanged surrounding test documentation; I read them as orientation. They describe CPU, synthetic and metadata checks for batching, prefix tenant partitioning, SSD prefix records, qualification and cluster service behavior.

This PR changes no runtime code, provider keys, attestation, coordinator WebSocket handling, prefix-cache storage or authorization. Its text does not weaken any threat-model claim for T-041, TB-007, TB-011 or TB-012. The tenant-partition and SSD-record checks are described as before, and the documented tests still state they are synthetic and do not replace hardware qualification.

One point for the next pass: the CI caching change moves cache-writing from pull requests to trusted-branch pushes. That reduces cache-poisoning exposure from untrusted PRs, a CI supply-chain concern the provided threat model does not cover. A PR-time audio gate skip could reduce test coverage, but master pushes run every component, so I see no security regression. The workflow files, scripts/ci-component-paths.py and build.md#ci-caching were not supplied. I could not verify that the actual CI configuration matches the documentation, so I flag that as an unverified contract rather than a finding.
